title: Cascode Stage
intro: The cascode places a common-gate transistor M2 on top of a common-source transistor M1. It multiplies the output resistance by about gm*ro.

blocks.source:
Rout = (1 + gm2*ro2)*ro1 + ro2  =  about gm2*ro2*ro1
Gain  = -Gm * Rout = about -gm1*ro1 * gm2*ro2

blocks.text: M2 shields the drain of M1 from output voltage swings: M1's drain moves by only Vout/(gm2*ro2), so channel-length modulation of M1 matters far less. The maximum gain climbs from gm*ro (about 20 to 50) to roughly (gm*ro)^2 (hundreds to thousands) for the same stage.

Both devices must stay in saturation, so the output swing shrinks. M1 needs Vov1 and M2 needs Vov2 plus their threshold arrangement: the minimum output voltage is about Vov1 + Vov2, and the bias for M2's gate has to be set accurately (VG2 = VGS2 + Vov1 for the widest swing).

To keep a high-gain stage working at low supply voltages, a PMOS cascode device can be 'folded' so the signal current from an NMOS input pair is steered into the opposite supply. It saves the stacked threshold voltage of the input device, at the expense of extra current and noise.

items: Telescopic cascode: highest gain, lowest power and noise, smallest swing and limited input common-mode range.
Folded cascode: more swing and input range, at the cost of extra current in the folding branch.

widget.title: Why cascoding matters: output current of a basic vs cascode mirror

blocks.text: The cascode mirror (flat line) plays the role of the cascode stage here: a much larger output resistance, so the current barely changes with Vout, but the curve only becomes flat above Vth + 2*Vov, which is the headroom cost.

blocks.title: Cascode output resistance
blocks.text: gm1 = gm2 = 1 mS, ro1 = ro2 = 50 kohm. Find Rout of the cascode and compare with a single transistor.
solution: Rout = (1 + gm2*ro2)*ro1 + ro2 = (1 + 50) * 50 kohm + 50 kohm = 2.6 Mohm.
A single device has ro = 50 kohm, so the cascode is 52 times higher.
blocks.answer: Rout is about 2.6 Mohm, 52 times a single device.

blocks.title: Cascode headroom
blocks.text: Vov1 = Vov2 = 0.2 V and VTH = 0.5 V. Find the gate bias VG2 that maximises output swing, and the minimum Vout that keeps both devices saturated.
solution: M1 needs VDS1 >= Vov1 = 0.2 V, so the source of M2 should sit at 0.2 V. M2 then has VGS2 = VTH + Vov2 = 0.7 V, so VG2 = 0.2 + 0.7 = 0.9 V.
M2 needs VDS2 >= Vov2 = 0.2 V, so Vout min = 0.2 + 0.2 = 0.4 V. Any higher VG2 pushes M2's source above 0.2 V and reduces swing.
blocks.answer: VG2 = 0.9 V; Vout min = Vov1 + Vov2 = 0.4 V.
